subject: Media Literacy
title: Surveillance Capitalism Explained
description: A short lesson to help you apply Surveillance Capitalism Explained.

hook.text: Google's first business model was selling ads. Its real model became selling predictions about your future behavior.

buildup.text: Surveillance capitalism, coined by Shoshana Zuboff, describes an economy built on extracting and selling human behavior data.

discovery.text: Companies collect behavioral data far beyond what's needed for services — the surplus is used to predict and influence you.

twist.text: The goal isn't just to predict your behavior. It's to shape it — nudging you toward outcomes profitable for advertisers.

climax.text: In surveillance capitalism, the product isn't what you buy. The product is the accurate prediction of what you'll do next.

punchline.text: They don't just watch what you do. They learn to make you do it.

quiz.question: What is the core product in surveillance capitalism?
options: Accurate predictions of human behavior sold to advertisers
